# captured 2026-09-22
# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/saml2aws
# args: 
usage: saml2aws [<flags>] <command> [<args> ...]

A command line tool to help with SAML access to the AWS token service.


Flags:
      --[no-]help              Show context-sensitive help (also try --help-long
                               and --help-man).
      --[no-]version           Show application version.
      --[no-]verbose           Enable verbose logging
      --[no-]quiet             silences logs
  -i, --provider=PROVIDER      This flag is obsolete. See:
                               https://github.com/Versent/saml2aws#configuring-idp-accounts
      --config=CONFIG          Path/filename of saml2aws config file (env:
                               SAML2AWS_CONFIGFILE) ($SAML2AWS_CONFIGFILE)
  -a, --idp-account="default"  The name of the configured IDP account. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_IDP_ACCOUNT) ($SAML2AWS_IDP_ACCOUNT)
      --idp-provider=IDP-PROVIDER  
                               The configured IDP provider. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_IDP_PROVIDER) ($SAML2AWS_IDP_PROVIDER)
      --browser-type=BROWSER-TYPE  
                               The configured browser type when the IDP provider
                               is set to Browser. if not set 'chromium'
                               will be used. (env: SAML2AWS_BROWSER_TYPE)
                               ($SAML2AWS_BROWSER_TYPE)
      --browser-executable-path=BROWSER-EXECUTABLE-PATH  
                               The configured browser full path when the
                               IDP provider is set to Browser. If set,
                               no browser download will be performed and
                               the executable path will be used instead.
                               (env: SAML2AWS_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH)
                               ($SAML2AWS_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH)
      --[no-]browser-autofill  Configures browser to autofill the username
                               and password. (env: SAML2AWS_BROWSER_AUTOFILL)
                               ($SAML2AWS_BROWSER_AUTOFILL)
      --mfa=MFA                The name of the mfa. (env: SAML2AWS_MFA)
                               ($SAML2AWS_MFA)
  -s, --[no-]skip-verify       Skip verification of server certificate. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_SKIP_VERIFY) ($SAML2AWS_SKIP_VERIFY)
      --url=URL                The URL of the SAML IDP server used to login.
                               (env: SAML2AWS_URL) ($SAML2AWS_URL)
      --username=USERNAME      The username used to login. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_USERNAME) ($SAML2AWS_USERNAME)
      --password=PASSWORD      The password used to login. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_PASSWORD) ($SAML2AWS_PASSWORD)
      --mfa-token=MFA-TOKEN    The current MFA token (supported in Keycloak,
                               ADFS, GoogleApps). (env: SAML2AWS_MFA_TOKEN)
                               ($SAML2AWS_MFA_TOKEN)
      --role=ROLE              The ARN of the role to assume. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_ROLE) ($SAML2AWS_ROLE)
      --policyfile=POLICYFILE  The file containing the supplemental
                               AssumeRole policy. (env: SAML2AWS_POLICY_FILE)
                               ($SAML2AWS_POLICY_FILE)
      --policyarns=POLICYARNS  The ARN of supplemental policies to restrict
                               the token. (env: SAML2AWS_POLICY_ARNS)
                               ($SAML2AWS_POLICY_ARNS)
      --aws-urn=AWS-URN        The URN used by SAML when you login. (env:
                               SAML2AWS_AWS_URN) ($SAML2AWS_AWS_URN)
      --[no-]skip-prompt       Skip prompting for parameters during login.
      --session-duration=SESSION-DURATION  
                               The duration of your AWS Session.
                               (env: SAML2AWS_SESSION_DURATION)
                               ($SAML2AWS_SESSION_DURATION)
      --[no-]disable-keychain  Do not use keychain at all. This will also
                               disable Okta sessions & remembering MFA
                               device. (env: SAML2AWS_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN)
                               ($SAML2AWS_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN)
  -r, --region=REGION          AWS region to use for API requests, e.g.
                               us-east-1, us-gov-west-1, cn-north-1 (env:
                               SAML2AWS_REGION) ($SAML2AWS_REGION)
      --prompter=PROMPTER      The prompter to use for user input (default,
                               pinentry)
      --kc-broker=KC-BROKER    The kc broker to use when authenticating via
                               keycloak

Commands:
help [<command>...]
    Show help.

configure [<flags>]
    Configure a new IDP account.

login [<flags>]
    Login to a SAML 2.0 IDP and convert the SAML assertion to an STS token.

exec [<flags>] [<command>...]
    Exec the supplied command with env vars from STS token.

console [<flags>]
    Console will open the aws console after logging in.

list-roles [<flags>]
    List available role ARNs.

script [<flags>]
    Emit a script that will export environment variables.
